content.value_statement: GraphQL APIs can become slow or unsafe when schemas, resolvers, and query limits are not designed carefully. This skill guides schema design, batching, federation, subscriptions, and client setup with practical safety controls.
actual_capabilities: Explains schema design choices, including types, nullability, and API contract boundaries.
Recommends resolver patterns that avoid N+1 database queries with DataLoader batching.
Highlights query depth, complexity, and introspection controls for safer production APIs.
Guides Apollo Server, Apollo Client, urql, subscriptions, federation, and GraphQL code generation decisions.
Identifies common GraphQL anti-patterns and safer implementation practices.
limitations: Does not include executable tooling, scripts, or automatic schema validation.
Does not replace review of application-specific authorization and data access rules.
Guidance depends on the GraphQL framework, database, and deployment environment.
Does not guarantee performance without load testing and production observability.

use_cases.title: Design a New GraphQL Schema
use_cases.description: Plan types, nullability, query shapes, and resolver boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Harden a Production API
use_cases.description: Review query depth, cost analysis, introspection, subscriptions, and field-level authorization controls.

use_cases.title: Integrate Client Data Fetching
use_cases.description: Choose Apollo Client or urql patterns for caching, generated types, and predictable component queries.

prompt_templates.title: Explain GraphQL Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how GraphQL schemas, queries, mutations, and resolvers work for a REST API team. Include the main safety concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Schema Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned GraphQL schema for type design, nullability, resolver ownership, and client usability. Highlight risky choices and improvements.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Resolver Performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this resolver design for N+1 queries, batching opportunities, cache boundaries, and DataLoader placement. Recommend a safer execution plan.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Federation and Controls
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a federated GraphQL architecture for these services. Include ownership boundaries, authorization checks, query complexity limits, and rollout risks.

output_examples.input: Review a product catalog GraphQL schema before implementation.
output: Checks whether product, price, inventory, and search fields have clear ownership.
Recommends explicit nullability and pagination for list fields.
Flags missing query depth and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Improve GraphQL resolver performance for an orders page.
output: Identifies likely N+1 lookup paths across orders, customers, and items.
Suggests DataLoader batching and request-scoped caching.
Separates authorization checks from batching concerns.

output_examples.input: Prepare a production hardening checklist for Apollo Server.
output: Covers introspection policy, depth limits, persisted queries, field authorization, and subscription cleanup.
Adds monitoring needs for slow operations and resolver latency.
Calls out tests needed before release.

best_practices: Design the schema as a stable contract before adding resolver logic.
Use DataLoader and query complexity limits for every production GraphQL API.
Enforce authorization inside resolvers and for sensitive fields.
anti_patterns: Allowing unlimited query depth or complexity in production.
Putting authorization only in schema directives without resolver checks.
Letting each resolver make independent database calls.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design, review, and improve GraphQL APIs, resolvers, client integration, and production safety controls.

faq.question: Does this skill run code?
faq.answer: No. It provides prompt guidance and does not include executable files.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with Apollo projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Apollo Server, Apollo Client, caching, and related client integration choices.

faq.question: Does it cover GraphQL security?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights introspection, query depth, complexity analysis, field authorization, and subscription cleanup.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing APIs?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to review schemas, resolvers, federation boundaries, and client integration risks.
